chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel, from Sadeer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Surah Al-Mulk is the Defender; it protects from the punishment of the grave. It is written in the Torah as Surah Al-Mulk. And whoever recites it during his night, he has abundant reward and goodness, and he will not be recorded among the heedless due to it.
And I bow (in prayer) with it after the last Isha prayer while I am seated, and indeed my father (peace be upon him) used to recite it during his day and his night.

And whoever recites it, when the Nakir and Nakeer (questioning angels) come to him in his grave from the direction of his legs, his legs will say to them: 'There is no way for you two to what is before me. This servant used to stand upon me and recite Surah Al-Mulk every day and night.'
And when they come to him from the direction of his chest/midsection, he will say to them: 'There is no way for you two to what is before me. This servant had sheltered Surah Al-Mulk inside me.'

And when they come to him from the direction of his tongue, he will say to them: 'There is no way for you two to what is before me. This servant used to recite by me, every day and night, Surah Al-Mulk.'

key_terms.سُورَةُ الْمُلْكِ: Surah Al-Mulk (The Sovereignty), Chapter 67 of the Quran
key_terms.نَاكِرٌ وَ نَكِيرٌ: Nakir and Nakeer, the two angels who question the deceased in the grave

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of reciting Surah Al-Mulk according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) identifies Surah Al-Mulk as 'Al-Mani'ah' (The Preventer), emphasizing its unique power to shield the believer from the punishment of the grave. The narration details a spiritual mechanism where the body's limbs testify to the consistent recitation of this Surah, effectively neutralizing the questioning angels Nakir and Nakeer. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the intercessory role of Quranic recitation in the Barzakh (intermediate realm) and the continuity of prophetic and imamic practice.
